title: Calibration sweep governance: multi-tenant isolation, artifact garbage collection, and validation gates
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Define and deliver a hardened lifecycle and governance model for calibration runs and their artifacts (FP8/INT8 sweeps). This covers: 1) multi-tenant isolation and RBAC for calibration creation, viewing, and artifact download; 2) deterministic garbage collection (GC) and TTL semantics for sweep artifacts and intermediate checkpoints; 3) validation/accuracy gating for auto-promote of quant profiles into model-serving catalogs; and 4) reconciliation path for orphaned/failed runs and cross-region artifact replication policy.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console shows explicit owner/team and tenant for every calibration run and artifact; UI and API enforce RBAC such that only authorized roles can start sweeps, delete artifacts, or download raw calibration tensors. 2) Policy-driven TTL (retention days) applied to runs/artifacts with both soft-delete and hard-delete phases; GC job respects dependencies (serving releases, audit logs). 3) Automated validation pipeline runs post-calibration and marks quant profiles with status: draft / validated / rejected; only 'validated' profiles are eligible for auto-promotion. 4) Orphaned artifacts (leftover after node failures or migration) are detected and reconciled by a background process with audit log entries and owner notifications. 5) End-to-end tests for a multi-tenant calibration sweep (FP8 and INT8) exercising RBAC, retention, GC, and validation gates pass in staging.
implementation_notes: Backend: extend calibration-run model with tenant_id, owner_email, retention_policy_id, and status fields (draft/queued/running/failed/complete/validated/archived). Add GC worker that runs daily and implements soft-delete (moved to 'archived' with 30-day grace by default) followed by hard-delete after TTL. Validation pipeline should compute accuracy deltas against baseline evals and produce a signed validation artifact (JSON) stored with the profile. Console: expose retention controls on run details, show validation badge and revision history. API: add /runs/{id}/reconcile endpoint for on-demand reconciliation triggered by ops. Audit: every deletion or reconciliation must emit an audit event to the customer's audit log bucket. Cross-region replication: use object-store replication for profiles and checksum verification for artifacts. Quant formats: ensure provenance includes quant scheme used (FP8/INT8/quant-profile-id) and RNG seeds used for calibration sampling.
migration_steps: 1) Backfill tenant_id for historical runs by joining run metadata with organizational mappings; 2) Run a dry-run GC pass in staging to collect metrics and false-positive rates; 3) Enable soft-delete + UI flag on staging for 2 cycles; 4) Enable hard-delete after stakeholder sign-off and metrics look stable. Provide a rollback plan to restore soft-deleted artifacts from cold backups for 14 days.
test_plan: - Integration tests: create calibration sweep as tenant A and ensure tenant B cannot access artifacts. - E2E accuracy test: run FP8 and INT8 sweeps, run validation pipeline and assert promotion rules. - Fault-injection: simulate worker crash leaving partial artifacts; run /reconcile and assert they are either completed or moved to 'failed' with audit log. - Retention test: set TTL to 14 days, create artifacts older than TTL and assert GC moves them to archived and then deletes after grace period.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): schema changes + GC worker dry-run; Phase 2 (limited production): opt-in tenants + monitoring dashboards; Phase 3 (wide): default TTL and automatic validation promotion enabled. Add feature flag 'calibration_governance_v1' to gate changes. Notify SRE and CS before Phase 2. Run a 48-hour monitoring window after each phase to watch for unexpected deletions.
open_questions: - What is RBAC mapping for external SSO groups vs console roles when granting 'artifact-download' permission? - Should validation thresholds (accuracy delta tolerances) be tenant-configurable or global? - For multi-tenant object-store replication, do we replicate all artifacts or only validated quant profiles? - Do we keep raw calibration tensors as part of default artifacts or move them to optional cold storage?
